To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

- Partial evaluation is an effective way to specialize concurrent programs - The specialization algorithm can be made more efficient by removing redundant synchronizations - The binding time analysis can be made more accurate by exploiting the fact that the communication primitives are synchronous.

1) Partial evaluation techniques can be applied to concurrent programs, 2) the basic constructs of a CSP like language can be handled, 3) a simple binding time analysis can be extended to handle concurrent constructs and 4) a simple specialization algorithm, that generates residual synchronizations, can be defined and proved correct.

(i) partial evaluation techniques can be applied to concurrent programs, (ii) the binding time analysis for the concurrent constructs is simple and effective, and (iii) partial evaluation of concurrent programs is a useful technique for improving the performance of concurrent systems.

the application of partial evaluation to concurrent languages.

the application of partial evaluation techniques to concurrent programs, and with the definition of a binding time analysis for a language that includes concurrent constructs.
